core_obligations: Choose the form and the lattice: take an R-universal Q-form of the Lie algebra of G, let the adjoint Q-group be the corresponding object, and define Gamma as the set of g whose adjoint image is integral, which is a lattice in G (proof lines 362-365).

Make the representation rational: given any finite-dimensional real representation rho, conjugate it so that the differential of rho maps the Q-form into the integral matrices, which is possible because the form is R-universal (proof lines 367-369).
Produce an invariant lattice: the corresponding representation of the universal cover is defined over Q, so there is an invariant Z-lattice in Q^n (proof lines 370-372).
Descend to Gamma: since the image contains a finite-index subgroup of rho(Gamma), that group also preserves a Z-lattice, so rho(Gamma) is conjugate into the integral matrices (proof lines 373-375).
proof_roadmap: 先取 R-universal 的 Q-形式，用 adjoint Q-群造出算术格 Gamma。
再把任意有限维实表示共轭到使微分落在整矩阵上；由 Q-形式的普遍性与不变 Z-格的存在性，最后把格下降到 Gamma 上，得 rho(Gamma) 共轭于整矩阵子群。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the arithmeticity corollary of the paper (author cor at source lines 115-125, label LattAppl): every connected semisimple Lie group with finite centre has a lattice Gamma such that G/Gamma has finite volume and every finite-dimensional real representation of G maps Gamma into a conjugate of the integral matrices. The proof (source lines 362-376) is the author's own, headed Proof of Corollary LattAppl, and it is short but it assembles three separate ingredients in the right order: the arithmetic lattice coming from the integral points of an adjoint group, the conjugation that makes the differential of an arbitrary real representation rational using the R-universal form, and the descent from the universal cover to a finite-index subgroup of the image (proof lines 367-375). The authors of the source cite this corollary as an application of the main theorem rather than as a new technique, and the card keeps the author's own level of detail. H2.
